conclusions.whole_whisper: Clear reproducible acoustic response: lower RMS, lower estimated periodic voicing, and altered pitch/prosody in both takes.
conclusions.scoped_whisper: No clear comparable whisper effect confined to the target phrase; target RMS changed only about half a dB and stayed highly periodic in both takes. Not validated as reliable scoped control.
conclusions.scoped_slow: Target duration changed by about 0% and 21% across two takes; not repeatably precise.
conclusions.pause: Inserted gap changed by about 0 and 1.12 seconds; not repeatably precise.
conclusions.happy_sad: Acoustic changes observed, but emotion correctness/naturalness cannot be established from these metrics alone; not marked as validated emotional performance.

method_limits: These are ASR/acoustic measurements, not a human listening verdict.
Two takes per condition characterize this installed quantized runtime only, not all Drama 3 deployments.
ASR word timestamps are coarse, approximately 80 ms. Character alignment is used only to estimate phrase boundaries.
Pitch/periodic-voicing estimates use 40 ms Hann-window autocorrelation, 10 ms hop, 70–500 Hz, correlation >=0.5; they are diagnostic, not a perceptual emotion classifier.
Raw audio is exported without loudness normalization so tag-driven level changes remain audible.
The production wrapper splits multi-sentence/long paired tags across chunks; subtitle text and the delivery field are not a complete tag-control integration.
